abstract: The paradigm of targeted therapeutics has shifted from static drug-target interactions to systemic absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) endpoints, dynamic transcriptomic perturbation signatures, and quantitative binding affinities, thereby amplifying the demand for multidimensional pharmacological atlases. In other words, it is necessary to bridge systemic safety profiles, cellular responses, and molecular interactions. However, such integrative data were inadequately covered by existing databases. In this study, DrugMAP was therefore substantially updated, which accumulated (i) 112 470 fine-grained ADMET endpoint profiles covering 126 endpoints for over 7680 drugs; (ii) 406 360 pharmacogenomic signatures for 3484 chemical perturbations and 11 033 molecules; and (iii) a quantitative bioactivity atlas covering molecular affinities, cellular sensitivity, and cytotoxicity for over 15 812 drugs and 4155 drug-interacting molecules. With the growing demand for quantitative pharmacology and the rapidly growing interest in AI-assisted drug discovery, DrugMAP is expected to act as an indispensable supplement to existing databases to facilitate drug discovery. DrugMAP is freely accessible at https://idrblab.org/drugmap/.
